scenarios.hypothesis: A controlled review should preserve one consistent identity interpretation across the documented transformation sequence used by policy and resolution.
scenarios.safe_oracle: Use a read-only synthetic fixture to compare recorded intermediate representations and the final benign resolved identity without any external action.
scenarios.positive_control: A neighboring synthetic record with the documented transformation order must remain consistent across policy and resolver observations.
scenarios.negative_control: A deliberately incomplete synthetic trace must remain unpromoted when the transform sequence or final identity evidence is missing.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop the review if any additional observation would require production data, sensitive records, or an uncontrolled external action.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After remediation, the same read-only fixture must produce the intended representation-to-identity relation while the neighboring valid control remains unchanged.
scenarios.representation_chain: Record the synthetic raw, parsed, decoded, normalized, policy, resolver, resolved-identity, and bound-object stages that actually exist.
scenarios.transform_order: Record the documented transformation order and compare only the controlled ordering needed to determine whether the original review state is stable.
scenarios.normalization_idempotence: Record whether the selected normalizer produces the same reviewed representation when applied again to its already-normalized synthetic output.
scenarios.equivalence_class: Record which synthetic representations are expected to be equivalent and which neighboring representations are expected to remain distinct.
scenarios.policy_key: Record the exact synthetic policy key used by the review and the documented semantics that define how it should identify the benign resource.
scenarios.resolver_input: Record the exact controlled resolver input and the documented rule used to interpret it inside the selected synthetic namespace context.
scenarios.resolved_identity: Record the benign fixture identity returned by the controlled resolver and bind that observation to a stable test identifier rather than display text alone.
scenarios.namespace_root: Record the synthetic namespace root or authority context shared by the policy and resolver observations so cross-root comparisons are not conflated.
scenarios.object_binding: Record whether the final review stage uses a stable bound object identity or a representation that may still be interpreted by a later layer.
scenarios.namespace_generation: Record the namespace generation or equivalent fixture-state marker used for every compared observation so stale and current records remain distinguishable.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Change only the recorded transformation order in the synthetic review while keeping fixture identity and namespace state otherwise unchanged.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Consider expected normalization, display-only formatting, fixture setup differences, or documented platform behavior before promoting the observation.
scenarios.evidence_level: Assign only the highest N0-N5 level directly supported by the synthetic representation trace, controls, resolver evidence, and namespace state.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: Cap the conclusion below any level that would require missing transform-order evidence, unknown object binding, or unobserved identity consequences.

scenarios.hypothesis: A consistency review should confirm that policy and resolution interpret the same synthetic child identifier under the same recorded namespace root or authority context.
scenarios.safe_oracle: Use a controlled read-only namespace fixture with benign identifiers to compare policy-root and resolver-root metadata without modifying any external resource.
scenarios.positive_control: A synthetic child record evaluated beneath the intended root must preserve the same reviewed identity and policy classification across both observations.
scenarios.negative_control: A synthetic record intentionally tagged with a different test root must remain classified as a separate namespace context rather than being merged by display similarity.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop before any review step would leave the synthetic namespace, inspect sensitive resources, or cause an uncontrolled service-side effect.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After remediation, the same controlled child record must remain bound to the intended root while the alternate-root negative control remains distinct.
scenarios.representation_chain: Record the child identifier representations from initial input through the policy key, resolver input, resolved identity, and any final bound-object record.
scenarios.transform_order: Record the transformations applied before root binding and after root binding so the review does not compare states produced by different ordering assumptions.
scenarios.normalization_idempotence: Record whether the normalized synthetic child identifier remains stable when the same reviewed normalization rule is applied a second time.
scenarios.equivalence_class: Record which child representations are intentionally equivalent within the selected root and which root-qualified identities must remain distinct.
scenarios.policy_key: Record the synthetic policy key together with its root or authority qualifier so the policy record cannot be interpreted outside its intended namespace context.
scenarios.resolver_input: Record the resolver input together with the same controlled root qualifier and the documented resolver semantics used by the fixture.
scenarios.resolved_identity: Record the benign resolved identity and the root-qualified fixture identifier that uniquely distinguishes it from the negative-control object.
scenarios.namespace_root: Record both policy and resolver namespace-root identifiers and explicitly state whether the fixture expects them to be identical or intentionally equivalent.
scenarios.object_binding: Record whether the reviewed result is a stable object identity scoped to the selected root or only a textual representation awaiting later interpretation.
scenarios.namespace_generation: Record the fixture generation associated with each root-qualified observation so comparisons never mix stale and current namespace snapshots.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Change only the namespace-root identifier in the synthetic record while holding the child representation and transformation sequence constant.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Consider intentional multi-root design, display-only similarity, stale namespace metadata, or expected configuration differences before promotion.
scenarios.evidence_level: Assign N0-N5 only from the observed root-qualified trace, benign identity evidence, controls, and the documented namespace semantics.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: Do not promote beyond the level supported when root provenance, resolver context, object identity, or namespace generation remains uncertain.

scenarios.hypothesis: A review should bind the checked synthetic name to a stable benign object record and the same namespace generation before interpreting identity continuity.
scenarios.safe_oracle: Use read-only synthetic object metadata and generation labels to compare the checked name record with the final benign object identity.
scenarios.positive_control: A current-generation synthetic name and its stable object record must retain the intended identity relationship throughout the review.
scenarios.negative_control: A deliberately stale synthetic generation record must remain labeled stale and must not be promoted as current object-binding evidence.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop the review if validating the next transition would require changing a real namespace, accessing sensitive data, or producing an uncontrolled effect.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After remediation, the same synthetic name and object record must remain consistently bound within one current generation while stale controls stay distinguishable.
scenarios.representation_chain: Record the synthetic name representations, policy key, resolver input, benign resolved identity, and final stable object record used for comparison.
scenarios.transform_order: Record the transformation sequence associated with the checked name before object binding and keep the same sequence for all control observations.
scenarios.normalization_idempotence: Record whether the selected normalization step remains stable across repeated review of the same current-generation synthetic name record.
scenarios.equivalence_class: Record the intended equivalence relationship between the current synthetic name and bound object while keeping stale-generation records separate.
scenarios.policy_key: Record the exact current-generation policy key and the fixture metadata that identifies which benign object it is intended to reference.
scenarios.resolver_input: Record the exact controlled resolver input and the generation/state marker associated with the lookup observation used by the review.
scenarios.resolved_identity: Record the benign object identity observed in the controlled fixture and the stable identifier used to distinguish it from neighboring objects.
scenarios.namespace_root: Record the synthetic namespace root or authority context in which both the checked name and bound object identity are interpreted.
scenarios.object_binding: Record the transition from reviewed name to stable benign object record and state whether later observations reuse that bound identity or only textual metadata.
scenarios.namespace_generation: Record the current and stale synthetic generation labels used by the review so evidence from different namespace states is never combined silently.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Change only the generation label in the synthetic review while preserving name, root, transform order, and neighboring fixture identities.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Consider stale metadata, expected propagation delay, duplicate observations, fixture refresh timing, or display-only differences before promotion.
scenarios.evidence_level: Assign the highest N0-N5 level directly supported by the generation-bound trace, object identity evidence, controls, and counterfactual result.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: Cap the finding whenever the current generation, object binding, root context, or resolver evidence is incomplete or internally inconsistent.
